changes in energy fluxes of meiotic and spermatogenic cells in the testis are rapidly translated into changes in cytosol [Ca2+] and pH.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the metabolic and ionic regulation of spermatogenic cell function.
the regulation of intracellular Ca2+, pHi and energy metabolism in rat spermatocytes and spermatids.
the study of the mechanisms that regulate energy metabolism and intracellular Ca2+/pH in meiotic and postmitotic germ cells.

changes in metabolic fluxes, in the absence of external Ca2+, are rapidly translated into changes in [Ca2+] and pHi in meiotic and post‐meiotic spermatocytes and spermatids.
the energy status of spermatogenic cells, which is highly dependent on external substrate availability, can be rapidly translated into changes in pHi, [Ca2+] and intracellular adenylate nucleotides.

The main takeaway from our work is that

changes in the metabolic flux of pachytene and round spermatogenic cells can be rapidly translated into changes in the intracellular pH and calcium levels of these cells, which are important for their normal development.
the energy metabolism and the regulation of pHi and Ca2+ in rat meiotic and post‐meiotic spermatocytes are highly dependent on the type of external substrate used for energy production.
